item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
My, these old posters are the type that only want the SCP Foundation (and especially S1) to be full of either creepy crap or stuff that can do something scary and hate the little unnatural or slightly unnerving anomalies that… are just interesting and harmless unless a special interest group is interested in it.

I had no problem with the terminology either, as it is to be expected that the Foundation will use words that you will probably not know, which makes it a good thing as long as it isn't overused (which in this article was not). Out of barochory, of which I didn't find a definition for, none were really that hard to look up, which makes Doctor Omicron's post sound like he'd rather stay on the elementary level of vocabulary.

Finally, I like this SCP because of the world building around Daevites, which I find as cool as Daedra! And I have a spot for disembodied (funny) heads and the dullahan. It makes a lot of sense why they react the most with women when you see they were grown-in-a-tree pets for matriarchs. I truly wonder if it would be worth reading their minds…

With all this, I give it a plus for support.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I enjoy what you've done here. The Daevite origin was well implemented, and I also appreciate the immediate reference in the beginning of the article. Waq Waq's use of her power to send a message (which I gathered from the discussion here was vindictive as per the previous iteration of this, but I'm trying to take the scip as-is) to all of her people for the rest of their civilization really meshes well with what I've interpreted as the Daevite culture and philosophy.

 However, I have a few issues with the scope of containment.
 -Hide

Population of SCP-392 instances is to be maintained at an upper limit of 100.

According to this article, a 10x10 grid of peach trees would be approximately 145 meters a side, requiring 21,025m2 of ground space.

(…)in a standard greenhouse sector(…)

Assuming this means an actual structure, that's a total of ~160,000m3, in addition to the necessary supports, walking space, and ceiling height. In my eyes, that's an excessive use of Foundation resources for what is ultimately a very safe anomaly.

The only reason I could accept such would be if these were the only extant instances of this species, and there would be no way to produce more. However, this -

Selected SCP-392 seeds are to be extracted and kept in cryonic storage at Bio Site-103.

As well as this -

(…)allowing the seed to be exposed to water and oxygen. Decomposed matter from the head will then serve as an organic fertiliser for germination.

Are very implicit that the Foundation is more than capable of reproducing this species in the event of a catastrophic loss. As it stands, I see no reason for this gross expenditure, and can not imagine that any Foundation budgetary committee would approve. Limiting the number of instances to 9, 16, or even 25 would drastically reduce the financial obligation involved.

Regarding Addendum 392-371, without the context provided by this thread, I could not understand the need for an automated containment system. The scip is about as Safe as it can get, so why would the Foundation expend even more resources when basic laborers could do the job?

Then I read this, and the context fell into place. While the previous iteration of the cross-testing and Keter Duty reference apparently came across as too direct, this version lacks enough of a hint to lead to your intended message. Perhaps something as simple as reformatting the footnote to include a blackboxed reference to a scip? That would have at least made me question the need for the proposal and associated experimentation.

 Again, however, I find the containment impractical.
 -Hide

The diagram at the top of this table gives a fair approximation of the root system of peach trees. Add that to a circle with dimensions large enough to hold the trees, and as per above, this is an incredibly large structure. Though 173 does not explicitly state the size of the containment chamber, I can not believe that it would be near the size that containment via these trees would require, and again taking into account additional space for the required mechanical systems. While I appreciate the idea, I'm not sure it works in current form. Perhaps the Foundation could be experimenting with keeping the heads alive and active when removed from the tree, which could then be used for the proposed 173 system in a more efficient manner?

Overall, I find the idea very novel. I can appreciate the narrative and history given here, and the concept itself would earn my upvote. However, the anomaly itself does not, in my mind, deserve the expansive treatment the Foundation is giving it.

No vote.

E: Vote amended accordingly. +1

item.title: Re: Lucky!
item.content:encoded:
Probability is more neutral; I just could not associate it with luck.

Drawing a straight flush, winning a lottery, or rolling a natural 20 are all events determined by simple probability, and are considered lucky. I am actually at a loss to think of something that is considered luck that doesn't have an element of randomness or unpredictability (or the illusion of randomness or unpredictibility).

Getting a slot in Series I is not particularly fortunate or desirable, just seizing it while it's there.

Perceived rarity and desirability usually creates value and I think has in this case. Besides there's the "achievement" that someone created for getting an article in every series, which I for one would like be able to claim, despite its totally arbitrary nature.

If anything, it's more of opportunism.

Well, yes but it isn't unusual for fortunate events with low probability that also require some effort or skill to exploit to be considered lucky.

item.title: Thanks, Attribution and Other Matters
item.content:encoded:
Take two!

Anyway, thank you to the reviewers of the previous and the current version for going through this.

This SCP involves SCP-140 by AssertiveRoland and SCP-2733 by ahbonjour.

+ show block
– hide block

As for why Daevites are mentioned right off the bat… the Foundation has knowledge over their culture in SCP-140. It would be criminal for them to not use it to expand their understanding. And the Foundation likely know more about Daevites than say… Sumerian, Olmec or Xia Dynasty…

And from an out-of-universe POV, it is tiring to see another SCP where the GoI reference is tacked at the rear end of the article.

The deviant purpose of 392 (as perceived by Daevites) was that it was kept as a reminder to a specific human lover way past his death.

And yes, the Chinese do have a practice of collecting enemy heads. A tree that provides human heads without the trouble of finding people to kill will be a boon.

And no, the Japanese have no such ritual in RL. The imperial court just took Ono's word for it and extrapolated it, who likely said it to justify the gifts from China (which is still technically correct). The monarchy (as an institution) would be obligated to perform many rituals as a head of state.

And… Argus-100 is a cross-test. I mean, this is a thing with eyes that can't blink…
